rationale: All five of my round-4 asks are addressed at 7404845f. I attacked the audited tuple live: on a real-git #239 topology (spec/S fast-forwarded onto main after a sibling PR merge; `git log --first-parent --merges spec/S` shows only the PR merge, the topo scan shows `Merge bead/lab-1.1` with second parent = X's tip) I wrote the complete round-5 tuple — binding pair, `…_reattest_merge_sha`, `…_second_parent`, `…_scanned_branch`, op, at, actor, corroboration — with one `bd update --metadata` on scratch bd 1.1.0 and read every key back. In that shape F1 (one candidate), F3 (surviving tip = second parent), F4 (x.txt present at tip) all pass and F2 has nothing to refuse, so nothing stops the forge: MF-3 would PASS without an operator vouch. That matches the stated residual. What the residual states inexactly is F2's provenance: the spec says the checks run 'from git and the panel scan, never from metadata' and that a forge 'is visible in the JSONL history', but the panel scan reads `reviews/*/panel.json`, which is UNTRACKED during a spec's life (this worktree's `git status` shows `?? .mindspec/specs/129-…/reviews/` right now; past specs' panel.json files are committed later), and its `round` is operator-supplied via `mindspec panel create … [--round N]`. A forger who also deletes the later-round registration dir, or lowers its `round`, defeats F2 with no history at all, so O3's round-2 shape (AC-11 ix-f) is reachable by a two-step forge. Only F1, F3 and F4 are git-derived. The rest is MINOR: the stale-checkout plan.md source, `reviewed_head_sha` as a git operand, and the cross-dir round convention.
concrete_changes_required: R4.2 residual and F2 provenance: state exactly which checks are git-derived (F1 subject scan, F3 surviving tip, F4 net-effect) and that F2 is derived from `reviews/*/panel.json`, which is agent-writable, not git-tracked during the spec's life (committed only later), and whose `round` is supplied by the operator/skill through `mindspec panel create … [--round N]`. Then restate the reach honestly: a forge that also removes or re-rounds a later unlanded registration reaches any single, reachable, source-named, non-reverted fallback merge whose surviving tip (if any) equals its second parent — including AC-11 (vii)'s O3 shape — and leaves no JSONL trace for the panel edit. Replace 'from git and the panel scan, never from metadata' and 'the write is visible in the JSONL history' with that statement, carry it into the ADR-0041 amendment item (i), and add an AC-11 leg (ix-g): the (ix-f) fixture with the round-2 registration dir deleted → MF-3 PASSES via the forged tuple, pinned as the documented reach (red if a future change claims F2 closes it).

F2 inputs, two pins: (a) `reviewed_head_sha` values reach `git merge-base --is-ancestor` as operands — require the existing `wellFormedGitObjectID` provenance gate (landed.go) before any git call, with a malformed value treated as a MALFORMED registration that fails F2 closed, and add an AC-11 leg with an option-like SHA. (b) Cross-dir rounds: `ms-panel-run` documents both the in-place re-bump and the per-round slug (`spec-050-bead2-r2`), and `--round` is optional on `panel create`; state what F2 assumes about a `-r2` dir registered without `--round 2` (a tie → fail closed, with the override/q9ea exits) and have the plan verify `panel create`'s default round, so a routine re-panel does not become a permanent F2 refusal.

R1.1 (c) plan source: the checkout-first order makes the classification depend on cwd when the invoking checkout is a bead worktree whose plan.md predates an amendment on `spec/<S>` (an adopted or added bead is N4 from that cwd and a member from the spec worktree), and `--emit-only` has no gate to catch it. Either prefer the committed `spec/<S>` blob whenever that branch exists and the checkout file differs (checkout only when the branch is absent), or print a one-line divergence notice (`plan.md in this checkout differs from spec/<S>; mapping used: <source>`) and pin it with an AC-1 fourth fixture: a stale bead-worktree plan.md with one fewer `## Bead` section than `spec/<S>`.

R1.2 N4 'half-mapped' and the `## Bead ` heading count: state that `PlanMapsBead` counts headings exactly as `extractBeadSectionRaw` does today (a `## Bead ` line inside a fenced code block counts), so selection and MF-1 cannot disagree even on that edge; pin it in `TestPlanMapsBead_AndPositional`.

findings.title: F2 is not git-derived: panel registrations are untracked, agent-writable files with an operator-supplied round, so the residual is understated
findings.detail: Live attack. Git: a scratch repo with main, spec/129-probe, bead/lab-1.1 merged as `Merge bead/lab-1.1` (M=d7a9abb…, second parent 671d758…), a sibling branch PR-merged into main, spec/S fast-forwarded to main; the first-parent scan sees only the PR merge, the topo scan sees M. bd: `bd update --metadata` wrote the binding pair plus `_reattest_{merge_sha,second_parent,scanned_branch,op,at,actor,corroboration}` and `bd show` returned all nine keys. Checks: F1 one candidate; F3 `bead/lab-1.1` == M^2; F4 `x.txt` = x1 at the tip; F2 nothing registered → nothing stops the forge, as the spec's residual says. Then the variant: round 2 on bead/lab-1.1 (B, not an ancestor of the tip) → F2 refuses only if a registration dir with round 2 and sha B is PRESENT in the scanned roots. Those dirs are `reviews/*/panel.json`: in this worktree `git status` shows `?? .mindspec/specs/129-readiness-tracker-honesty/reviews/` (untracked), while older specs' panel.json files are tracked only because they were committed later; `round` comes from `mindspec panel create … [--round N]`. So the forger deletes the round-2 dir or edits its `round` to 1 and F2 passes, with no JSONL history for that half of the forge. The spec's sentences 'from git and the panel scan, never from metadata' and 'detected by inspection: the write is visible in the JSONL history' are therefore not exact; AC-11 (ix-f)'s guarantee holds only against a forger who leaves panel.json alone. The stated reach should be: any single, reachable, source-named, non-reverted fallback merge whose surviving tip, if any, equals its second parent. That is a text correction, not a redesign — no git-derived substitute for F2 exists, and the operator vouch via reattest remains the honest bound.

findings.title: F2 operand provenance and cross-dir round semantics are unstated
findings.detail: `reviewed_head_sha` is agent-writable panel.json data and F2 passes it to `git merge-base --is-ancestor`; landed.go already gates binding SHAs with `wellFormedGitObjectID` before any git use (ADR-0042), and F2 should say the same. Separately, `ms-panel-run` documents two conventions — in-place re-bump of `round`/`reviewed_head_sha`, and a per-round slug `…-r2` — and `panel create`'s `--round` is optional, so a `-r2` dir registered at the default round ties the stale dir's round and F2 fails closed on an ordinary history. Safe direction, but it should be named with its exits and the default verified.

findings.title: Checkout-first plan.md source can mis-map from a stale bead worktree
findings.detail: `workspace.FindRoot(cwd)` from inside a bead worktree resolves that worktree, whose `plan.md` is the bead branch's copy; after an adopt-lattice or plan amendment on `spec/<S>` the copy under-maps, so `next --spec S --emit-only` run there names a real plan bead as N4 while the spec worktree selects it — a cwd-dependent answer with no gate to catch it on the emit-only path. `EvaluateReadiness` has the same root dependence today, so the claim path stays self-consistent; the ask is to prefer the committed blob or print a divergence notice.

findings.title: Attacks that did not land
findings.detail: Anchor masquerade: a registration whose `reviewed_head_sha` is an ancestor of the candidate's second parent is by construction in the tip's history (the second parent is reachable from the tip), so an unlanded later round cannot be an anchor's ancestor; the equal-OR-ancestor anchor is right for #233's tree-identical `complete` commit, and I could not build a shape where it admits unlanded work (verified on the fixture: A is an ancestor of M^2, B is not an ancestor of the tip). Stale audit: the executor's `MergeMetadata` rewrite leaves the old tuple naming M1 while the binding names M2 → inequality → nothing granted (AC-11 xii). PlanMapsBead: AND plus positional count equals `evaluateMF1`'s precondition; a mapped bead that still fails MF-1 on content (placeholder AC, empty key_file_paths) is a legitimate NOT-READY, not a selection lie; a half-mapped N (chunk without section, or section without chunk) is N4 and MF-1 would refuse it anyway, so nothing is wrongly hidden. Classification order (N2a, N2c, N4, N2b, N1, N3) is consistent with the blocking/informational split. N4 positional with lineage E → MF-1 refusal → scoped MF-1 override claims it; with no lineage → refused at selection with GateReadiness never called: consistent with R1.8. No worktree was created; the scratch git repo and bd database under r5/F3 are removed.
